### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `32750307f14dc720e4ebe726a40f262457d88109` — the merge of head `70d74f15cb27f411a2ab6a9fe748d8671e6be21b` into base `556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 32750307f14dc720e4ebe726a40f262457d88109 && git checkout 32750307f14dc720e4ebe726a40f262457d88109
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc 70d74f15cb27f411a2ab6a9fe748d8671e6be21b && git checkout -B drift-repro 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc && git merge --no-ff 70d74f15cb27f411a2ab6a9fe748d8671e6be21b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 556f3230cdd43caa6a263a35c2133e1e9fbfbefc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d94c12dd70c9fe1a35cb871477bf99614932cd99`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/import-multi-value-match-key.test.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-multi-value-match-key.test.ts + packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/package.json, packages/core/src/utils/import-field-meta.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts, packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs; `.changeset/27465-multi-value-match-key.md` read under ② only (prose)

Face: `narrowing` (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` declared on the PR body and the changeset; no schema and no governed path in the file list). Reviewed read-only against `origin/main` `ad3a640e35` (merge-base `d4ff1a025f`), the card's body and all three comments (6491237090, 6496194949, 6497566983), the PR body and file list, and the net diff `origin/main...d94c12dd`. Check-runs on the head read at 2026-10-29T13:11Z: 40 runs, 12 `success`, 0 `failure`, 20 `in_progress` (Build Core, Test Core 1-8, the four Type Check jobs, six Lint jobs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI), 8 `skipped`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `PR-body guards` concluded `success`. No gate had concluded red at that reading; the verdict below does not rest on the in-progress ones. Record rendered 2026-10-29T13:17Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing at the two import doors — right.** `prepareImportRequest` (`import-prepare.ts`, after the field map resolves) refuses an `update` / `upsert` request whose `matchFields`, or whose named mapping's `upsertKey` when that supplied the key, names a field the rule flags, with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and a message naming each field with its kind. Both routes go through it (`data-action-routes.ts:448` sync, `:562` async jobs), so the async door refuses before any job row is written. Measured at base per the PR and consistent with the card: such a request answered `200` with every row failed, so the narrowed set is one no caller could use.
- **Runner-level narrowing of `runImport` (`@objectstack/core`) — right.** In `update` / `upsert` the runner fails every row with `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `field` = the first flagged key, before `rowsSharingKey` and before any `coerceRow` (so before the lookup cells' reference resolution and any `findData`). `VALIDATION_ERROR` is the standard catalog's generic 400 (`errors.zod.ts:55`), and `INVALID_REQUEST` is not registered under `@objectstack/core` in the ledger, so not stamping it from the runner is right. (The PR body's phrase that `INVALID_REQUEST` is registered to `@objectstack/rest` only is inaccurate — the ledger carries it under several packages — but the conclusion stands; see ④.)
- **Public-surface widening of `@objectstack/core` — present, and NOT declared.** `multiValueMatchKeyRefusal` is a new `export function` in `import-runner.ts`, and `packages/core/src/index.ts:104` re-exports that module whole (`export * from './utils/import-runner.js'`), which is the `.` entry of `packages/core/package.json` `exports`. The symbol is therefore published from `@objectstack/core`'s root, with a signature (`(matchFields, metaMap, keyedBy?) → { fields, message } | undefined`) that consumers can pin. The os-dev-report itself says "exported from @objectstack/core" and the PR body says "exported beside `runImport`". `@objectstack/rest`'s index does not re-export it (`rest/src/index.ts:35` re-exports `runImport` alone), so the widening is on `core` only.
- **Declaration line — WRONG.** `Clause-②` answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (`clause2-line.mjs`; CONTRIBUTING Human Minimum item 5: accept set or public surface). A diff that narrows an accept set and adds a published export is the arm vocabulary's `yes (narrowing)` ("a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read."). The tree's own precedent is exact: commit `67cf0b1add` (#26947) declared `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — … and @objectstack/rest gains one export (DATA_RECORD_READ_PARAMS) so both hosts read one set`. This PR declares `no (narrowing) — … Nothing is widened.` on both the PR body and the changeset, which misstates the public-surface half. **Must-fix on the declaration line** (PR body and changeset): `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, naming the new `@objectstack/core` export beside the narrowing. The face stays `narrowing` either way (the `(narrowing)` arm decides it), so this record's tier and scope are unchanged by the correction.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** No key an author writes changes; `packages/spec` is untouched.
- **No governed path, no schema** in the file list — right; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27465-multi-value-match-key.md`: `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `@objectstack/core: patch` — **right**. Under the level axis the gate enforces (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3), the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The packages moved are the two the diff touches. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`.
- The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), with the before/now/remedy a breaking entry owes; nothing an author writes is removed or renamed, so no migration or tombstone is owed — right.
- The `Clause-②:` line in the changeset is the same wrong `no (narrowing)` as the PR body (①); correcting it to `yes (narrowing)` changes no bump: `yes` takes `minor` only when the kind is a protocol kind, and here the kind is `none`. The `!` in the title and the banner match the narrowing.

### ③ Boundary flags

The os-dev-report (6497566983) lists no `open_questions`; its two `out_of_scope_findings` and the seat claim's flags, each answered or escalated:

1. **Multi-value criterion (which fields count).** Answered — right. The rule asks the spec, never a hand list: `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` (`json`, `composite`, `repeater`, `record`, `location`, `address`, `vector`; `field-value.zod.ts:350`) and `isMultiValueField` (`MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` = `multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`; `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` = `select`, `radio`, `lookup`, `user`, `file`, `image` when `multiple: true`; `:385`). `ExportFieldMeta.multiple` is `f.multiple === true` from the object schema (`import-field-meta.ts:32`, `:104`), so `metaMap` carries exactly the bit the spec reads. The report's measurement (multiselect and tags failed every row at base like the lookup; json failed with `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`) puts the non-lookup kinds in on evidence, not analogy; a single-value lookup, a single-value file field and every scalar stay legal keys. This is rule one as the seat picked it from the triage ("a multi-value lookup cannot be a match key … the import door refuses it with a prescription"), applied to the whole JSON-column population.
2. **Insert mode not judged.** Answered — right. `runImport` reads the key only in `findExisting` (reached only when `writeMode !== 'insert'`) and `rowsSharingKey` (returns early on insert), so an insert's `matchFields` is dead input; refusing it would narrow a request that works today. Pinned by both test files.
3. **Runner guard on the connector-pull path.** Answered — right. `connector-pull.ts:293-297` reads `writeMode` and `matchFields` straight off the mapping artifact and calls `runImport` at `:417` with `metaMap: buildFieldMetaMap(schema)` (`:423`), without `prepareImportRequest`; the guard fires there with the same `multiple`-bearing map and fails every row before any read or write, returning the summary the pull already returns. `admin-import-users.ts:565` goes through `prepareImportRequest` with a scalar key (`email` / `phone_number`), so it is unaffected.
4. **Spec `matchFields` describe silent on the refusal** (`export.zod.ts:295-306`; outside the file surface, carrier: seat). Escalated to the seat: the describe should say that a field holding a list or a structured value (a `multiple: true` lookup, a multiselect, a json field) is refused as a key with `INVALID_REQUEST`. Not advertising a capability the runtime lacks, so not a defect on this diff — a should-fix follow-up, filed by the seat as a `domain:server` card or folded into the next spec touch.
5. **The ui half** (`ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx` `matchable` still offers multi-value fields; triage's rule one has two halves). Escalated to the seat: the card thread followed `os-dev.md` and filed nothing; the draft body is at the project files `issue-27465/ui-card-draft.md`. The seat files the `domain:ui` card linking back to #27465 before this card closes; until it lands, ticking such a field meets this door's 400 instead of 28 row errors, which satisfies the triage's "⛔ never a raw SQL error to the user" on its own.
6. **Branch name** `claude/project-thread-138abn` (not `claude/issue-27465-…`): recorded in the claim as a measured platform exception; `PR-body guards` concluded `success`.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree, file by file, against the cited code on `main` and the accepted scenario (triage 6491237090: pick one rule, never a raw SQL error; the seat: a multi-value field cannot be a match key, the door refuses with a prescription).

- **`packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts` — holds.** The refusal sits after the field map resolves (`:677-693` on `main`) and before `refuseUnknownMappingTargets`, on the dry run and the commit alike, since both routes arrive through this function. `matchFieldsFrom` is set only in the `upsertKey` fallback branch (`:588-590`), so an explicit request key is named `matchFields` and a mapping-supplied key names the mapping. Tried: `update` and `upsert` with the lookup alone, beside a scalar, and as a later ordered key set — all refused (the rule flattens every set); `insert` with the same key — not judged, right; a name absent from the map — judged by nobody, consistent with `coerceRow` passing it through as a string (no array ever reaches the filter, so no SQL error); a failed schema read leaves `metaMap` empty, so neither layer refuses, but then no cell coerces to an array either — pre-existing behaviour, not a regression. A mixed key names every offending field once, in key order. The message carries the prescription and no tracker number.
- **`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` — holds.** `multiValueMatchKeyRefusal` asks `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` first, then `isMultiValueField({ type, multiple })`, exactly the spec's two arbiters; `typeof meta?.type !== 'string'` skips a typeless entry. The guard runs at the top of the async body, before `rowsSharingKey()` (which calls `coerceRow` → `resolveRef` → `findData`), so nothing is read or written; `errCount = rows.length` precedes the one `snapshot(rows.length)`, and the return shape `{ ...snapshot, ok, results, cancelled, undoLog? }` matches the normal return at `:1497-1499` with every slot of `results` filled, so the async job's `patch` sees `error_count` and `processed_rows` once. `field`, `code` and `error` are the `ImportRowResult` keys the spec declares (`ImportRowResultSchema`), and `errors` is correctly absent on a refused write. Tried: dry run — same refusal, no `validateData`; the connector pull — guard fires (③.3); zero rows — one progress call with `processed: 0`, harmless. `rowsSharingKey` needs no change because it is never reached with such a key.
- **`packages/rest/src/import-multi-value-match-key.test.ts` — holds.** Real route over a real `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), the card's object; every refusal pin asserts `400`, `INVALID_REQUEST`, each field named, no `results`, no `findData` / `updateData` / `createManyData`, and the stored rows unchanged; the preservation pins (scalar key upserts and writes the lookup as a column; insert not judged) guard the narrowing's edge. Covers upsert and update, commit and dry run, mixed and ordered keys, multiselect/tags/json, and a named mapping's `upsertKey`.
- **`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-multi-value-match-key.test.ts` — holds.** Pins the rule on all eleven refused kinds with the named kind, the five legal-key boundaries (scalar, single-value lookup, single-value file, unknown name, ordered legal sets), and `runImport` in three modes with the protocol double proving nothing was called; the `keyedBy` prefix is pinned on the mapping spelling.
- **PR body prose (no tree change) — should-fix.** The sentence "`INVALID_REQUEST` is registered to `@objectstack/rest` only in the error-code ledger" is wrong on the ledger (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts` registers it under `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/service-i18n`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` too); the point that holds is that it is not registered under `@objectstack/core`. Reword when the declaration line is corrected.

No must-fix in the four scope files. The one must-fix is the declaration (①): `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with "Nothing is widened" misses the new `@objectstack/core` export. Correct both the PR body and the changeset to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, name the export beside the narrowing, keep both bumps `patch`, and the next head is reviewable on this record's findings with ③.4 and ③.5 carried by the seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Carried over unchanged** from record 6497763460: the accept-set narrowing at the two import doors (`prepareImportRequest`, sync and async-job routes), the runner-level narrowing of `runImport` with `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no governed path and no schema in the file list. (beside runImport, through export * from './utils/import-runner.js')`. ### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree. The four code/test files are byte-identical to the head record 6497763460 judged (`import-prepare.ts` blob `f6f96ed81b`, `import-runner.ts` blob `eb4cdc46a0`, both test files unchanged in the range), so their ④ — door after the field map resolves, both routes, `upsertKey` fallback named by mapping, insert not judged, unknown name judged by nobody, mixed and ordered keys flattened, the runner guard ahead of `rowsSharingKey` / `coerceRow` / `findData`, return shape matching the normal return — **carries over unchanged; all four hold.**
